findings.title: Speculative decoding never runs: transformers rejects assisted generation for Qwen3_5 (stateful), the app swallows the error silently and still reports "spec-decode: on"
findings.evidence: libsrc/transformers/transformers/models/qwen3_5/modeling_qwen3_5.py:812 `_is_stateful = True` (base class of every Qwen3_5 model). generation/utils.py:1578-1583: `if self._is_stateful: raise ValueError(f"assisted generation is not supported with stateful models, such as {self.__class__.__name__}")`, called at :2486, before `streamer.put` (:2599). app.py:293-307 catches `(TypeError, ValueError)`; the message contains none of the drop names, so `last_err = err; break`, then attempt 2 runs without `assistant_model`. Nothing is printed. app.py:567 `use_spec = bool(speculative and SPEC_AVAILABLE)` and :661 `spec-decode: {'on' if use_spec else 'off'}`; :852 "up to ~2x faster decode"; README.md:19 same claim. Repro SCRATCH/work/inference-perf/repro_spec.py (fake model raising the exact message): two generate calls, second without assistant_model, stdout ''. Native MTP is also unavailable: modeling_qwen3_5.py:807 `_keys_to_ignore_on_load_unexpected = [r"^mtp.*"]`; MTPCandidateGenerator wants `num_mtp_layers` (candidate_generator.py:1438) but config has `mtp_num_hidden_layers`; use_mtp/prompt-lookup hit the same stateful check.
findings.impact: The advertised ~2x speed-up is 0x. The Qwen3.5-2B draft still costs ~17 s of boot, ~4.4 GB of the 22.3 GB pack copied to the GPU on every lease (every tool round), and VRAM. Every request also pays one failed generate() setup. Users and the owner are told spec-decode is on.
findings.recommendation: Remove the draft (DRAFT_ID, mount, load block, checkbox, README claim) until transformers supports rollback for hybrid caches. If kept for the future, gate at import: `SPEC_AVAILABLE = draft is not None and not getattr(model, '_is_stateful', False)` and skip loading the draft when the target is stateful. In `_generate_kwargs` log every fallback: `print(f'app: assisted generation rejected, plain decode: {err}', flush=True)` and never retry on errors other than the known early-validation ones. Report truth in stats from a flag set where the fallback happens (or the static check above), not from the checkbox. Real speculative decoding for this model exists only via the bundled MTP head in vLLM/SGLang (see inference-perf-8).
findings.how_to_verify: Run SCRATCH/work/inference-perf/repro_spec.py; or on the Space add a print in the except branch of _generate_kwargs and send one request with Speculative decoding checked: the ValueError text above appears once per request.

findings.title: Every boot re-reads 54.7 GB of bf16 over the model mount and re-quantizes to NF4 on CPU (~4.5 min); a pre-quantized NF4 checkpoint would make boot ~1-1.5 min and end the race with the ~300 s restart
findings.evidence: app.py:96-103 `from_pretrained(_model_source(), quantization_config=bnb, device_map="cuda", ...)` on the bf16 repo. live_runlog: 23:33:52 'flash-attn not installed' -> 23:36:16 first 'Loading weights' tick = 144 s silent (234 s on the first boot); loop 23:36:16->23:38:03 = 107 s at ~8 it/s for the 845 LM tensors, 35-75 it/s for unquantized vision ones. Silent phase (inferred): modeling_utils.py:4507-4509 `if load_config.disable_mmap or _is_on_hf_mount(file): ... merged_state_dict.update(_safe_load_bytes(_fh.read()))` reads every shard fully into RAM when /proc/mounts device is 'hf-mount' (:293-315), incl. the discarded 849 MB model-auxiliary.safetensors (mtp.*). Quantize path integrations/bitsandbytes.py:57 `bnb.nn.Params4bit(value,...).to(value.device)`; deserialize path exists (:88 `Params4bit.from_prequantized`). spaces/zero/torch/bitsandbytes.py: for bnb>=0.46 `_patch = lambda: None`, nothing forbids pre-quantized. Hub search: no heretic-ara bnb repo exists; `unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-unsloth-bnb-4bit` is the base model.
findings.impact: Boot takes 4m29s-4m57s and two of four observed boots were killed at ~5m00-5m10 (F4), so the Space can loop for 10-15 min before serving. Peak host RAM is >= 55 GB state dict plus the 18 GB quantized copy. Every restart, dependency bump or Dev Mode refresh pays this again.
findings.recommendation: Quantize once offline (GPU box or machine with >=64 GB RAM), using the text-only class so vision and MTP tensors are dropped: `m = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(MODEL_ID, quantization_config=bnb, dtype=torch.bfloat16); m.save_pretrained(out, max_shard_size='4GB'); tokenizer.save_pretrained(out)` plus chat_template.jinja and generation_config.json; upload to a private model repo (an empty private `Prekzursil/Qwen3.8-27B-heretic-ara-NF4` already exists) and mount that repo at /models instead of the bf16 one. In app.py drop `quantization_config` when the mounted config already has one. Expected: ~18 GB read (50-75 s at the observed 235-380 MB/s) and no quantize loop. Small shards bound the per-file full read. Log `_is_on_hf_mount(path)` at boot to confirm the mechanism.
findings.how_to_verify: In Dev Mode run `grep /models /proc/mounts` (device 'hf-mount' confirms the eager full-file read). After switching, the log gap between 'model source' and 'target loaded' should fall from ~270 s to under 90 s and 'Loading weights' should run at hundreds of it/s.

findings.title: presence_penalty is a no-op: never placed in gen_kw and transformers 5.16.1 has no such option, so the "Instruct (official)" preset and the API field do not do what they say
findings.evidence: app.py:326 `presence_penalty=1.5,` is a parameter of `_gpu_impl`, but the kwargs built at :354-363 contain only max_new_tokens, do_sample, temperature, top_p, top_k, min_p, repetition_penalty, pad_token_id; presence_penalty is never referenced again in the function. `grep -rn presence_penalty libsrc/transformers/transformers/generation/` returns nothing, so generate() could not honour it anyway; the drop list at app.py:296-301 naming 'presence_penalty' is dead code. UI: :833-840 slider 'Presence penalty' with info 'Qwen instruct default is 1.5'; presets :700-712 'Instruct (official)' presence_penalty=1.5; README.md:33 'Presets now follow the official Qwen3.8 sampling guidance ... instruct = temp 0.7 / top_p 0.8 / presence 1.5'; openai_protocol.py:346-348 parses the API field. The Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B card does recommend presence_penalty=1.5 for instruct mode and 0.0 for thinking.
findings.impact: Non-thinking chats and API calls run without the penalty Qwen recommends to suppress repetition loops, which on a quota-metered lease means wasted GPU seconds when the model loops. The slider, preset label and API field mislead users into thinking they control something.
findings.recommendation:
Implement it as a logits processor with OpenAI/vLLM semantics (flat subtraction for tokens already generated, prompt excluded):
```python
class PresencePenalty(LogitsProcessor):
    def __init__(self, penalty, prompt_len): self.p, self.n = penalty, prompt_len
    def __call__(self, input_ids, scores):
        gen = input_ids[:, self.n:]
        if gen.shape[1] == 0: return scores
        mask = torch.zeros_like(scores, dtype=torch.bool).scatter_(1, gen, True)
        return scores - self.p * mask
```
In `_gpu_impl`: `if float(presence_penalty) > 0: gen_kw['logits_processor'] = LogitsProcessorList([PresencePenalty(float(presence_penalty), encoded['input_ids'].shape[1])])`. Add a CPU unit test with a toy scores tensor. If not implemented, remove the slider, the preset key, the README sentence and the API field rather than keep a placebo.
findings.how_to_verify: grep -n presence_penalty app.py: no hit inside the gen_kw dict. After the fix, a unit test asserts scores of previously generated ids drop by exactly the penalty and prompt-only ids are untouched.

findings.title: Gated DeltaNet layers (48 of 64) run the pure-PyTorch fallback: no fla, causal-conv1d or kernels package in requirements.txt, and 5.16.1 emits no warning
findings.evidence: requirements.txt lists transformers, accelerate, bitsandbytes, sentencepiece, protobuf, pillow, torchvision, pypdf, hf_transfer only. modeling_qwen3_5.py:199/219 `@use_kernel_func_from_hub_with_fallback("causal_conv1d_update"|"causal_conv1d_fn", "causal_conv1d")`, :248/:330 same for `chunk_gated_delta_rule` / `fused_recurrent_gated_delta_rule` with package "fla". hub_kernels.py:826-835: 'priority is 1. Hf kernels (if requested) 2. Original package 3. Torch only path'; on import failure `implementation = torch_function`, silently (no 'fast path' string exists in the file). Fallback prefill (:249-327) casts q,k,v,beta,g to float32 for the whole sequence, runs `for i in range(1, chunk_size)` plus a Python loop over every 64-token chunk per layer; decode (:331-380) is ~12 small fp32 ops plus cat/copy/conv1d/slice/act for the conv, per layer per token. Config: 48 linear_attention layers. Hub: kernels-community/mamba-ssm has builds torch28..torch212; kernels-community/fla was NOT found as a model repo.
findings.impact: Prefill of long prompts (file bench, tool results, preserved thinking) is slow and needs roughly 230 KB/token of extra fp32 scratch per layer call; decode pays ~1,000+ extra kernel launches per token in a loop that already looks launch-bound (owner measured ~9 tok/s versus a bandwidth bound near 100). All of it is billed ZeroGPU time.
findings.recommendation: Step 1 (no nvcc needed): add `flash-linear-attention` to requirements.txt; it is pure Python/Triton and transformers picks it up via `importlib.import_module('fla')`. Triton JIT/autotune then runs inside the first lease after each boot, so add a tiny warm-up generate or raise `overhead` in `_estimate` for the first call, and point TRITON_CACHE_DIR at persistent storage if available. Step 2: causal-conv1d has no generic PyPI wheel; pin the matching prebuilt wheel URL from the Dao-AILab GitHub releases for the image's torch/CUDA/cp312, or add `kernels` and load with `use_kernels=True` (mapping hub_kernels.py:169-225) after confirming the fla kernel repo resolves. Print at boot which implementation each of the four functions resolved to.
findings.how_to_verify: At boot: `import transformers.models.qwen3_5.modeling_qwen3_5 as m; print(m.torch_chunk_gated_delta_rule.__wrapped__.__module__)` style check, or simply `importlib.util.find_spec('fla')` is None today. Then time prefill of a 16K-token prompt and 256 decode tokens before and after adding the package.

findings.title: The advertised 262K context does not fit on `large` as coded: KV is 64 KiB/token (16 GiB at 262K) and the un-chunked prefill scratch is several times larger; chunked prefill is available but unused
findings.evidence: app.py:814-821 slider max 262144 with info 'Full 262K context available'. Model config.json (Hub, read-only): 64 layers, 16 `full_attention`, num_key_value_heads 4, head_dim 256, bf16 -> 16*2*4*256*2 = 65,536 B/token: 2 GiB at 32K, 8 GiB at 131K, 16 GiB at 262K; GDN state is fixed (~151 MiB fp32 + ~4 MiB conv). Weights: log 'ZeroGPU tensors packing 22.3G' (target ~17.9 GB + draft ~4.4 GB). README.md:18: large = 48 GB, xlarge = 96 GB (spaces configs.json: RTX PRO 6000, memory 101973950464). Free on large ~24 GB. Un-chunked prefill transient (estimate): MLP ~105 KB/token (3 x 17408 x 2 B) plus torch GDN fallback ~233 KB/token fp32 (inference-perf-4). generate supports `prefill_chunk_size` (generation/utils.py:3941-3985, 'Chunked prefill (for very large contexts)'); app.py never sets it.
findings.impact: Estimated ceiling today is roughly 70-80K prompt tokens on `large` before CUDA OOM inside a paid lease (about 110K with fla), and 262K does not fit on xlarge either without chunking. The user sees an error after queueing and burning quota. Separately, DURATION_CAP=600 s limits output to ~5-13K new tokens, so a 262,144 max-new-tokens slider is unreachable.
findings.recommendation: Pass `prefill_chunk_size=8192` in gen_kw whenever the prompt exceeds ~8K tokens: scratch becomes constant (~3 GB) and, with the draft removed, KV for 262K (16 GiB) then fits beside ~18 GB of weights on `large`. Count prompt tokens in `_encode_messages` and reject or trim before taking a lease when `prompt + max_new_tokens` exceeds a per-size budget measured once (log `torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated()` at the end of `_gpu_impl`). Change the slider ceiling and info text to the measured budget; include prefill time (tokens / measured prefill rate) in `_estimate` instead of `min(30, chars/3000)`.
findings.how_to_verify: Log input length and torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated() per request; send one 64K-token and one 100K-token prompt on large with and without prefill_chunk_size=8192 and compare peak memory and OOM behaviour.

findings.title: No decode or prefill rate is ever measured; TOK_PER_SEC=22 is a guess that contradicts the owner's own 9.2 tok/s and drives the lease estimate
findings.evidence: app.py:71 `TOK_PER_SEC = 22.0  # conservative 27B NF4 decode (Blackwell large runs faster)`; :232 `gen = new_tokens / TOK_PER_SEC`; :820 UI text '~22 tok/s measured'. The only number with a source is the commit message of 99ed760 ('measured-rate estimator (9.2 tok/s)', scout F1) and that code is not in any revision. Stats line app.py:657-668 reports `wall` (queue + lease setup + tool time + all rounds) and an approximate `completion tokens` from re-tokenizing text, never tokens/s. `_gpu_impl` (:315-397) knows prompt length, first-token time and generated pieces but records none of them. No log line in live_runlog.txt reports speed (F5).
findings.impact: Nobody can tell whether any optimisation here helps or hurts, and the duration estimate is off by about 2.4x if 9.2 tok/s is true: a 4096-token answer needs ~445 s, not 186 s, so leases end mid-answer; at 600 s the hard ceiling is ~5.5K tokens while presets request 8192 and 16384.
findings.recommendation: Instrument `_gpu_impl`: record `t0`, time of first piece (TTFT = transfer + prefill), count generated tokens with a `StoppingCriteria`/`LogitsProcessor` counter or `len(input_ids)` delta, and print one line per call: `app: gen prompt=%d new=%d ttft=%.1fs decode=%.1f tok/s peak=%.1fGB impl=%s spec=%s`. Yield the same numbers as a final sentinel so the stats block and the API `usage` can show real tok/s. Keep an exponentially weighted average per gpu_size in the main process and feed it to `_estimate` (with a safety factor) instead of the constant. This is also the acceptance test for inference-perf-1, -4 and -8.
findings.how_to_verify: grep -n 'tok/s' app.py shows only UI strings and the constant. After the change, the runtime log contains one 'app: gen ...' line per GPU call.

findings.title: AutoModelForImageTextToText loads a vision tower (and NF4-quantizes it) for a text-only app; the text-only causal LM class is a supported load path
findings.evidence: app.py:96 and :130 use `AutoModelForImageTextToText` for target and draft while :114-115 deliberately loads only a text tokenizer. models/auto/modeling_auto.py:835 `("qwen3_5", "Qwen3_5ForCausalLM"),  # VLM compatibility`; modeling_qwen3_5.py:1584 `_keys_to_ignore_on_load_unexpected = [r"^mtp.*", r"^model.visual.*"]`; conversion_mapping.py:978 `"qwen3_5_text": [PrefixChange(prefix_to_remove="language_model", model_prefix="model")]`. Checkpoint index (idx.json): 333 `model.visual.*` tensors; vision_config depth 27, hidden 1152, intermediate 4304 -> ~0.46 B params. The log shows tensors 846-1184 (vision) loading at 28-75 it/s, i.e. they are loaded, and bnb converts their nn.Linear modules too.
findings.impact: Small: about 0.25-0.9 GB less VRAM and per-lease transfer for the target, more for the draft if it is kept, a simpler forward (no multimodal rope-index and placeholder handling per step), and a smaller pre-quantized checkpoint. Worth doing only together with inference-perf-2.
findings.recommendation: Switch both loads to `AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(...)` (resolves to Qwen3_5ForCausalLM with the text config) and drop `trust_remote_code=True`, which is unnecessary for a natively supported architecture. Verify once that `model.config.model_type == 'qwen3_5_text'`, that the load report lists no missing keys, and that greedy output for a fixed prompt matches the current class. Produce the NF4 checkpoint of inference-perf-2 from this class so the saved repo has no vision or MTP tensors.
findings.how_to_verify: Load the 2B draft repo locally on CPU with AutoModelForCausalLM and AutoModelForImageTextToText, compare greedy tokens for one prompt and parameter counts; check the loading report for missing/unexpected keys.

findings.title: Serving options ranked: bnb blocks torch.compile and AoTI; compile-friendly and MTP-capable alternatives exist but the large wins are off ZeroGPU
findings.evidence: quantizers/base.py:261-263 `is_compileable ... return False`, overridden only in compressed_tensors, finegrained_fp8, gemma, nvfp4, torchao; generation/utils.py:2137-2142 requires a non-Dynamic compilable cache and `hf_quantizer.is_compileable`. spaces/zero/torch/aoti.py is torch.export per module (`aoti_capture`/`aoti_compile`/`aoti_patch`, calls `unwrap_tensor_subclass_parameters`, i.e. torchao-style weights), built for fixed-shape blocks, not a growing hybrid cache. Checkpoint carries MTP weights: idx.json has 15 `mtp.*` tensors in model-auxiliary.safetensors (849 MB), ignored by transformers. Confirmed Hub repos: magiccodingman/Qwen3.8-27B-heretic-ara-fp8, fermicalva/Qwen3.8-27B-heretic-ara-MTP-FP8, JC1DA/Qwen3.8-27B-heretic-ara-INT4-INT8-GPTQ (gptqmodel 7.3.4, 23.2 GB), mradermacher/Qwen3.8-27B-heretic-ara-GGUF, cygnal/Qwen3.8-27B-heretic-ara-Q4_K_M-MTP-GGUF; base: Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8, unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-unsloth-bnb-4bit, cyankiwi/Qwen3.8-27B-AWQ-INT4. vLLM recipe (recipes.vllm.ai/Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B): `--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'`, acceptance 0.77-0.90.
findings.impact: The owner is tuning a stack whose ceiling is low: eager PyTorch plus bnb gemv on a launch-bound loop. Knowing which steps are cheap and ZeroGPU-safe versus which need a different host avoids spending weeks on compile experiments that bill quota on every cold worker.
findings.recommendation: Ranked (gain / effort / risk / ZeroGPU): 1) pre-quantized NF4: boot 4.5 -> ~1.5 min / M / low / yes. 2) drop draft: -20% per-lease transfer, -17 s boot / S / none / yes. 3) fla (+causal-conv1d): prefill several x, decode est. 10-20% / M / medium (Triton JIT in lease) / yes. 4) prefill_chunk_size: enables long prompts / S / low / yes. 5) `bnb_4bit_use_double_quant=False`: few % decode for ~1.1 GB (inferred) / S / low / yes. 6) FP8 heretic checkpoint via finegrained_fp8 on Blackwell: faster prefill, compileable, 29 GB weights / M / medium (third-party quant, more transfer) / yes on large. 7) static cache + torch.compile or AoTI on a compileable quant: up to 2-3x decode / L / high (compile billed per cold worker, hybrid cache export) / uncertain. 8) dedicated GPU with vLLM or SGLang + FP8/AWQ + MTP: 5-10x / M / cost / no.
findings.how_to_verify: Use the per-call log line from inference-perf-6 as the benchmark; apply items 1-5 one at a time and compare ttft and decode tok/s on the same three prompts (short, 16K, 64K).

findings.title: Hygiene: dead flash-attention chain, fragile retry logic in _generate_kwargs, stray files and stale claims
findings.evidence: app.py:86-92: FA variants are tried only if `import flash_attn` succeeds; the image never has it (log: 'flash-attn not installed in image; using sdpa'), so README.md:19 'flash-attention chain (fa3 -> fa2 -> sdpa)' describes dead code. modeling_utils.py:1862-1868 shows transformers already falls back to `kernels-community/flash-attn2` when `kernels` is installed, and attention-implementation errors surface at model init, before weights load, so the suspected 'full reload per failed impl' cost does not hold. Only 16 of 64 layers use softmax attention, so FA gain over SDPA is small. app.py:288-312: the second attempt reuses the same streamer (a failure after generation/utils.py:2599 `streamer.put(input_ids)` would make the retry stream the prompt as output); `if last_err is None: return None` returns without generating after four drops; `last_err` is never reset. idx.json (112 KB copy of the safetensors index) is referenced by no file. app.py:78 double quant adds a dequant per linear per token (inferred).
findings.impact: No user-visible failure today, but the README and UI promise optimisations that do not exist, and the retry wrapper can turn a mid-generation error into duplicated or prompt-echo output instead of a clean failure.
findings.recommendation: Delete the FA chain and load once with `attn_implementation="sdpa"`; remove the README sentence. Replace `_generate_kwargs` with one validated call: build kwargs from an explicit allow-list, call `model.generate` once, and let errors propagate to the existing `err_box` path; if a retry is kept, create a fresh streamer per attempt and only retry errors raised before the first token. Remove idx.json and runlog_tail.txt from the Space repo. Benchmark `bnb_4bit_use_double_quant=False` when regenerating the NF4 checkpoint and keep whichever is faster within the VRAM budget.
findings.how_to_verify: grep -rn idx.json in the repo returns nothing; read app.py:83-109 and 278-312 against the cited transformers lines.

findings.title: Lease estimator assumes 22 tok/s: at the 9.2 tok/s the owner measured, every preset's lease ends before its own max_new_tokens can be produced
findings.evidence: app.py:70-71 `DURATION_CAP = 600` / `TOK_PER_SEC = 22.0`; app.py:230-235 `prefill = min(30.0, chars / 3000.0)` ... `gen = new_tokens / TOK_PER_SEC` ... `return int(max(60, min(DURATION_CAP, requested)))`. Computed (work/gpu-lease/lease_math.py), requested s / needed s at 9.2 tok/s / tokens before lease end: Instruct+Precise 4096: 253/470/2.1K; Thinking+Creative 8192: 543/915/4.8K; Deep think 16384 xlarge: 600/1806/5.3K; Fast draft 1024: 85/136/552; slider max 262144: 600/28519 (7.9 h)/5.3K. spaces 0.51.3 stretches non-xlarge leases on Blackwell (client.py:112-113 `if gpu_size != 'xlarge': duration_seconds *= zerogpu_config['duration_factor']`, configs.json RTX PRO 6000 `"duration_factor": 1.5`): then 3.3K / 7.3K / 943 tokens; still short. 9.2 tok/s is only a commit-message figure (F5).
findings.impact: Any reply longer than ~50% of the preset budget dies mid-stream with 'GPU task aborted'. Deep think can deliver about a third of its 16K budget. A whole PRO day (2400 s) buys ~22K output tokens on large, ~11K on xlarge; one full Deep-think answer (1806 s x2 = 3612 quota-s) exceeds the daily quota. Credits: ~5.5K tokens per $1 on large.
findings.recommendation: Set TOK_PER_SEC from measurement (start at 9.2, then EMA per gpu_size, see gpu-lease-8). Replace the 30 s prefill cap with prompt_tokens / measured prefill rate. ' + reasoning_content + '
</think>

findings.title: Stop / disconnect releases the lease but never stops model.generate: a zombie generation keeps running in the reusable worker
findings.evidence: Parent: wrappers.py:404-408 `except GeneratorExit: worker.stop_event.set(); raise`. Worker: wrappers.py:452-454 `if stop_event.is_set(): gen.close(); break`, then l.465 `res_queue.put(EndResult())` -> parent l.366-368 `workers[nvidia_index] = worker; release()`. gen.close() only raises GeneratorExit at app.py:395 `yield piece`; the generate thread started at app.py:383 `Thread(target=_target, daemon=True).start()` has no stop signal (no stopping_criteria in gen_kw app.py:354-363, no finally). The worker is kept and reused when `worker.process.is_alive() and schedule_response.idle` (wrappers.py:335). Gradio does close the generator on cancel (gradio/utils.py:910-914, queueing.py:1111-1121).
findings.impact: After Stop on a 16K-token run the old generate keeps decoding for up to ~30 min (hours at the 262K slider max) on a GPU the scheduler considers free. If the next request reuses the warm worker, two generate() calls share the GPU, halving a speed the lease already overestimates, so the new reply is cut even sooner.
findings.recommendation:
Tie generation to the consumer's lifetime:
```python
class _StopOnEvent(StoppingCriteria):
    def __init__(s, ev): s.ev = ev
    def __call__(s, ids, scores, **kw):
        return torch.full((ids.shape[0],), s.ev.is_set(), device=ids.device, dtype=torch.bool)
stop_ev = threading.Event()
gen_kw["stopping_criteria"] = StoppingCriteriaList([_StopOnEvent(stop_ev)])
th = Thread(target=_target, daemon=True); th.start()
try:
    ...consumer loop...
finally:
    stop_ev.set(); th.join(timeout=30)
```
The join keeps EndResult (and thus release) from being sent while the GPU is still busy. Interface verified: stopping_criteria.py:618-626.
findings.how_to_verify: Add `print('app: generate thread exited', flush=True)` in _target's finally. Start a long generation, press Stop, watch the log: today the line appears minutes later (or never); after the fix within about a second.

Forward the caller's identity: pass the starlette `request` into the generate function and set the context immediately before the GPU call in the same thread:

```python
def api_generate(*, request=None, **kw):

        LocalContext.request.set(request)   # has .headers.get('x-ip-token')
    yield from _gpu_generate(...)
```
(spaces only needs `request.headers.get`, client.py:311-319.) Add a `threading.Semaphore(1)` around API generation so it cannot stack leases, and return HTTP 429 with the scheduler's message on quota errors.

findings.title: python_eval child inherits every Space secret (HF_TOKEN, NF4_UPLOAD_TOKEN), has no resource limits, runs in the app directory, and its timeout leaves orphans
findings.evidence: web_tools.py:440-445 `subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-I", "-c", src], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=PYTHON_TIMEOUT)` -- no env=, cwd=, preexec_fn, or process group. Repro (work/security-tools/pyeval.py, canary values): child printed `{'HF_TOKEN': 'hf_FAKE_canary_for_repro', 'NF4_UPLOAD_TOKEN': 'hf_FAKE_write_canary'}`; cwd = parent's cwd and writable; `RLIMIT_AS/CPU/NPROC/FSIZE: (-1, -1)`; after `error: timed out after 2s` a detached grandchild still wrote its marker file 5 s later (subprocess.run kills only the direct child). Tools run in the main Gradio process (app.py:772 at HEAD f88b120, :642 at 17dce0c), so the env is the full Space env incl. SPACES_ZERO_DEVICE_API_URL. README.md:48 sells `-I` as "isolated mode"; -I only ignores PYTHON* vars and user site.
findings.impact: PRIVATE: only bites when the owner ticks the box, but then one prompt-injected page (web tools default ON) can print os.environ and post it out; NF4_UPLOAD_TOKEN is write-scoped. A snippet can also OOM the container (5-min NF4 reboot) or edit app.py on disk. PUBLIC: critical, unauthenticated RCE plus token theft.
findings.recommendation: Verified sketch in work/security-tools/pyeval_fix.py: `Popen(..., cwd=tmpdir, start_new_session=True, env={'PATH':'/usr/bin:/bin','HOME':tmp,'LANG':'C.UTF-8'}, preexec_fn=_limits, stderr=STDOUT)` where _limits sets RLIMIT_AS 1 GiB, RLIMIT_CPU=timeout, RLIMIT_FSIZE 8 MiB, RLIMIT_NPROC 0; on TimeoutExpired `os.killpg(p.pid, SIGKILL)`. Local result: env = ['HOME','LANG','PATH'], fork -> BlockingIOError, 3 GiB alloc -> MemoryError, spin killed at 3.0 s, normal snippet fine. Add a server-side gate so a boolean alone cannot enable it: `allow_python = bool(python_eval) and os.environ.get('ALLOW_PYTHON_EVAL') == '1'`. Fix the README wording. This is limits, not a sandbox: the network stays open from the child.
findings.how_to_verify: python3 SCRATCH/work/security-tools/pyeval.py SCRATCH/work/security-tools/src (shows inherited canaries, unlimited rlimits, surviving grandchild); then pyeval_fix.py for the hardened behaviour.

findings.evidence: web_tools.py:110-114: urlopen follows redirects, then `final = resp.geturl() ... if _reject_private_host_soft(fhost): raise` -- after the fact. web_tools.py:84 `socket.getaddrinfo(hostname, None)` is a separate lookup from the one urllib does at connect. agent_tools.py:459-462 pdf_read calls `_ur.urlopen` directly. web_tools.py:62-69 omits `not ip.is_global`. No-socket repro (ssrf_redirect_toctou.py, ssrf_guard.py): web_fetch public->302->169.254.169.254 returned `error: redirect to non-public host blocked` but `requests actually issued: [public, 'http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/iam/']`; chain public->10.0.0.5->public returned HTTP 200 body; rebinding: `lookups: [93.184.216.34, 127.0.0.1]`, `connect target: 127.0.0.1:7860`; `http://100.64.0.1/ -> ALLOWED`; `:22`, `:6379` allowed; redirect replayed `Authorization: Bearer fc-SECRETKEY` to attacker.example. Decimal/hex/octal, ::ffff:, 0.0.0.0, trailing dot, userinfo: all correctly blocked.
findings.impact: PRIVATE: a prompt-injected page can make the container issue GETs to internal addresses (blind), read localhost:7860 via rebinding (the app is unauthenticated behind HF's proxy, so POST /v1/chat/completions burns GPU quota), and README.md:49 promises protection that does not hold. PUBLIC: high, any visitor drives it directly.
findings.recommendation: One opener for every outbound call (incl. pdf_read and Firecrawl); verified stdlib sketch in work/security-tools/fix_sketch.py: connection classes whose connect() resolves once, rejects `not ip.is_global` (also unwrap ipv4_mapped), then sets `self._create_connection` to dial that literal IP (TLS still uses server_hostname=host); an HTTPRedirectHandler whose redirect_request validates scheme/port of newurl before the hop, max 5 hops, and pops Authorization when the host changes. Repro after fix: one lookup, connect target = validated IP. Restrict ports to 80/443/8080/8443. Alternative: `safehttpx` (already installed, gradio METADATA:43 `Requires-Dist: safehttpx<0.2.0,>=0.1.7`) pins the IP but is GET-only. Add tests for redirect, rebinding, CGNAT.

findings.title: Interaction: correcting TOK_PER_SEC alone (gpu-lease-1 / inference-perf-6) turns 'cut off mid-answer' into 'refused at admission'; reservation must be decoupled from max_new_tokens
findings.evidence: space-latest/app.py:333-336 `gen = new_tokens / TOK_PER_SEC` ... `requested = (overhead + prefill + gen * think_mult + media_overhead) * 1.2` / `min(DURATION_CAP, requested)`: the lease is sized from the token CEILING, not the expected answer. libsrc/spaces/spaces/zero/client.py:112-113 `if gpu_size != 'xlarge': duration_seconds *= zerogpu_config['duration_factor']` (configs.json Blackwell entry: `"duration_factor": 1.5`), and client.py:186-187 admission compares `({requested}s requested vs. {res.left}s left)`. At 9.2 tok/s the default Instruct preset (4096) asks (25+445)*1.2=564 s, x1.5 = 846 s of a 2400 s day; Thinking/Creative hit the 600 s cap = 900 s. The agent loop repeats that request up to 8 times per turn (app.py:705-727).
findings.impact: After roughly 25 minutes of real use, every preset is rejected with 'quota exceeded' even when the answer would be 50 tokens, and long reservations also lower queue priority. The estimator fix as proposed trades one failure for another.
findings.recommendation: Treat gpu-lease-3 (short chained leases) as the primary fix and the estimator as chunk sizing only: reserve a fixed slice (e.g. 120-150 s, about 1K tokens at the measured rate), stop on a token budget inside the worker, and chain while the model has not emitted EOS. Add an explicit `lease_s` kwarg that `_estimate` honours. On a gr.Error whose message matches `(\d+)s requested vs\. (\d+)s left`, retry once with `lease_s = left/1.5 - 5` and a proportionally smaller token budget instead of printing the generic truncation text. Give tool rounds their own small budget (a tool call is <200 tokens).
findings.how_to_verify: Run work/gpu-lease/lease_math.py with TOK=9.2 and multiply large-size results by 1.5; compare with 2400 s. On the Space, log `requested` and the quota error text for one day.

findings.title: HEAD NF4 export runs inside the first GPU lease with no time budget, and its one-shot flag lives in a forked worker, so a failed export repeats on every new worker
findings.evidence: space-latest/app.py:198 `_NF4_STATE = {"pending": os.environ.get("NF4_EXPORT") == "1", "saved": False}`; :230-232 `if not _NF4_STATE["pending"] or _NF4_STATE["saved"]...: return` / `_NF4_STATE["saved"] = True`; :238 `model.save_pretrained(out, safe_serialization=True)`; :448 called at the top of `_gpu_impl`; `_estimate` (:321-336) has no term for it. libsrc/spaces/spaces/zero/wrappers.py:59 `multiprocessing.get_context('fork')`, :337-341 a worker is reused only `if worker is not None and worker.process.is_alive() and schedule_response.idle`, else `Worker(thread_wrapper, ...)` forks the main process again, where `saved` is still False. The upload is a daemon thread of that worker (:221). :208 falls back to `HF_TOKEN` when `NF4_UPLOAD_TOKEN` is absent.
findings.impact: With secret NF4_EXPORT=1 (set now, A7) the first call must write ~16 GB inside a 60-250 s lease before producing a token; if the lease expires the worker dies, the flag is lost and the next call tries again. Chat is unusable until the secret is removed, and quota is spent on saves.
findings.recommendation: Do not export from the serving Space. Produce the checkpoint once offline (a GPU box or a one-off paid job the owner starts by hand) with a short script: load with the same BitsAndBytesConfig, `save_pretrained`, `upload_folder`, using a fine-grained token limited to that one repo and never stored as a Space secret. Then delete `_maybe_nf4_export_inline`, `_upload_nf4_async`, and the NF4_EXPORT / NF4_UPLOAD_TOKEN secrets. Decide the model class first (see coverage notes): a bnb checkpoint freezes the class layout and the quantized vision tower.

findings.title: Interaction: lease chaining / Continue (gpu-lease-3, chat-loop-ui-8) cannot go through the chat template for this model; continue at token level
findings.evidence:
Model chat_template.jinja (copy at SCRATCH/work/chat-loop-ui/chat_template.jinja):103 `{%- set content = render_content(message.content, true)|trim %}` and :117 `'<|im_start|>' + message.role + '
<think>
' + reasoning_content + '
</think>

' + content`. Reasoning comes only from `message.reasoning_content`; a `</think>` is always written before content; content is trimmed. libsrc/transformers/transformers/utils/chat_template_utils.py:546 `continue_final_message if isinstance(continue_final_message, str) else "content"`, :599 cuts the render at the tag. So continuing a reply that stopped inside thinking closes the think block early (the model then answers without finishing its reasoning), and continuing visible text loses trailing newlines/indentation, which corrupts code blocks.
findings.impact: The proposed fix for long outputs would silently degrade answers exactly in the thinking presets that need chaining most, and would damage formatting at every chunk boundary.
findings.recommendation: Have the worker yield the prompt length and the generated token ids at the end of each chunk (a final dict record after the text pieces). For the next lease pass `input_ids = prompt_ids + generated_ids` straight to `model.generate`, skipping `apply_chat_template`. This is exact, avoids retokenization drift at the seam, and also gives the token counts needed for the tok/s record in gpu-lease-8. Keep `continue_final_message` only for a user-initiated Continue on a finished, non-thinking turn.
findings.how_to_verify: Render the template with jinja2 (as work/chat-loop-ui/repro_context.py does) for a final assistant message with reasoning_content='abc' and content='' plus the CONTINUE tag, and inspect where `</think>` lands.

findings.title: Highest-leverage change nobody proposed: a stub-engine mode so the whole app (UI loop, API, MCP) boots on CPU in seconds and can be tested before every push
findings.evidence: space-latest/app.py:122-123 `tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(...)` / `model = _load_target()` run at import, so nothing in app.py can be imported or tested; tests/ has no test that touches app.py (chat-loop-ui coverage notes). Every confirmed high-severity chat-loop defect is glue that only shows end to end: bench_turn metadata stripped by Gradio (chat-loop-ui-1), `request=gr.Request()` never injected (chat-loop-ui-2), blank user text under multimodal (critic-2), and A2's four undefined names that a second agent pushed to production with the Space now down (A1).
findings.impact: Today each change costs a 5-minute boot plus real quota to try, so changes go out untested; commit messages describe behaviour that never existed (F1). A CPU stub makes each of these bugs a failing test in under ten seconds.
findings.recommendation: Split app.py: `engine.py` (model load, `_encode_messages`, `_gpu_impl`, `@spaces.GPU` wrappers) and `ui.py` (chat loop, presets, Blocks). In app.py: `engine = engine_stub if os.environ.get('QWEN_STUB') == '1' else engine_real`. The stub yields scripted pieces (a plain reply, a `<tool_call>` for list_files, an unterminated `<think>`), records the `msgs` it received, and can raise a fake gr.Error('ZeroGPU quota exceeded'). Tests drive `demo` with gradio_client on localhost: turn 2 must contain turn 1's tool results; two sessions must get different benches; POST /v1/chat/completions streams and stops on disconnect. Gate pushes on `pyflakes` + unittest + this smoke test.
findings.how_to_verify: `python -c "import app"` on a laptop today: it starts downloading a 27B model. After the split, `QWEN_STUB=1 python app.py` should serve the UI locally in seconds.

INTERACTION NOTES FOR THE LEAD
1. inference-perf-7 (load the text-only CausalLM class) conflicts with the direction at HEAD, which adds image and video input through AutoProcessor. The owner has to pick one. The choice must be made BEFORE the NF4 checkpoint of inference-perf-2 is produced, because a serialized bnb checkpoint fixes the class layout and the quantized vision tower, and cannot be re-quantized. Same ordering applies to dropping double quant.
2. inference-perf-5's chunked prefill does not work with the ImageTextToText class (verifier note), so it also depends on decision 1.
3. gpu-lease-2: with speculative decoding impossible, the 2B bf16 draft is about 4-5 GB of the 22.3 GB pack that is copied to the GPU whenever a worker is not reused. Removing the draft load is a free win and should ship with the UI label fix. Also, `_gpu_large` and `_gpu_xlarge` each keep their own `workers` dict (wrappers.py:313), so switching size always forks a new worker and pays the full transfer again.
4. chat-loop-ui-2 fix (per-session bench) plus `save_history=True`: a conversation restored from localStorage after a refresh will reference bench files that no longer exist, and once chat-loop-ui-1 is fixed the replayed tool results will describe files the new bench does not have. Either key the bench by a conversation id stored with the history, or show a clear 'bench is empty, re-upload' notice.
5. gpu-lease-5 fix: the spaces stop_event is not visible to the task; the practical hook is GeneratorExit at `yield piece` in `_gpu_impl` setting a threading.Event that a StoppingCriteria checks. The same criteria object can enforce the per-chunk token budget of critic-1 and critic-4.
6. gpu-lease-8 stats must travel from the worker to the main process as a yielded record, since the worker is a fork (wrappers.py:59) and anything it writes to module globals is invisible to the main process. critic-3 is the same mistake in the owner's code.
7. openai-api-1/-6 and critic-1 share a cause: all lease policy lives in `_estimate`. A single `lease_s` kwarg and one `LeasePolicy` helper in the main process would serve the UI loop, the API and the retry-on-quota path.

Still unproven without a GPU run; test on a duplicate Space, not on production.
